findings.claim: release-gate.yml Check deprecation-ramp invariant step enforces the one-MINOR elapsed ramp but does NOT enforce that target_release is a MAJOR release. VERSIONING.md step 3 states explicitly: 'the MAJOR bump is the breaking-change vehicle.' A same-major deprecations.yaml entry with target_release v1.2.0 (MINOR) announced at v1.0.0 satisfies cand_minor - ann_minor = 2 >= 1 and would pass the gate, allowing a MINOR-release removal of a public surface in violation of the semver contract.
findings.evidence: release-gate.yml lines 173-184: 'if ann_major == cand_major: if (cand_minor - ann_minor) < 1: violations.append(...)' — no guard on cand_minor == 0. VERSIONING.md §Deprecation ramp step 3: 'Release N+M (the MAJOR after the next MINOR): old surface is removed; the MAJOR bump is the breaking-change vehicle.' VERSIONING.md §Semver guarantee table: 'MAJOR (vX.0.0) | Breaking changes ... | Mandatory'. schemas/deprecations.schema.json target_release pattern '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' — no constraint requiring MINOR == 0.
findings.impact: An operator who inadvertently authors a deprecations.yaml entry with a MINOR target_release will receive a gate-green on the tag-cut even though removing a public surface in a MINOR release violates the VERSIONING.md contract. Adopters relying on the MAJOR-only removal guarantee could face a silent breaking change at a MINOR boundary without SCP machine enforcement catching it.
findings.mitigation: In the if ann_major == cand_major: branch of Check deprecation-ramp invariant, add a secondary guard: if cand_minor != 0 or cand_patch != 0: append violation with reason 'target_release {target} is a MINOR/PATCH release — breaking changes must be removed in a MAJOR release per policies/VERSIONING.md step 3; update target_release to v{cand_major+1}.0.0.' This is a two-line addition. Alternatively file as TF-020H3rg-003 if preferred, but the fix is small enough to resolve in this fix-round.

When the first rule-deprecate proposal is filed, operators have no implementation path for this doctrinal promise.
